Team wants token/sec baselines, streaming behavior and fallback model options. Agreed to run POC and share security docs.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-04 15:00 UTC | Duration: 46m | Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Carlos Mendes (SE), Aisha Khan (CSM); Maya Iyer (Triton Head of ML), Ravi Patel (Infra), Sam Ortiz (CTO), Liu Chen (SRE)

00:00 - Lena (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros - i'm lena from redwood, carlos is our solutions eng, aisha on CS. you folks?
00:12 - Maya (Triton): hi maya here, head of ml. ravi infra, sam cto and liu sres. we've been running transformers in prod and want to understand latency/throughput tradeoffs for inference, and whether we go hosted or reserved dedicated infra.
00:28 - Carlos (Redwood SE): great. can you give a sense of current traffic and SLOs? p95 numbers, payload sizes, typical concurrency, streaming needs?
00:40 - Ravi (Triton): sure, rough numbers: peak concurrent ~80 requests, typical burst to 150 for a couple minutes. typical prompt is user prompt + 200 tokens system, target response around 300-500 tokens. our p95 target is ideally < 300ms for 256 tokens, but we know that might be tough so we're interested in tradeoffs. streaming is important for UX because the UI displays progressive text.
01:05 - Lena: ok that helps. p95 <300ms for 256 tokens with concurrency 80-150 and streaming - that pushes toward Dedicated or private with optimized kernels, but let's talk specifics. Carlos, do you want to walk through runtime behavior?
01:18 - Carlos: yeah. a couple things to call out: latency depends on model size, quantization, sequence length, batching and whether requests hit KV cache. streaming also impacts tail because we flush tokens more frequently. on our hosted tier we have multiple model variants; for guaranteed p95 we usually recommend dedicated pools if customers need consistent throughput under high concurrency. but often HostED + smart routing + prefix caching can meet many SLOs.
01:40 - Sam (Triton): two quick clarifs: when you say kv cache, you mean last-token key-value cache for decoder states? also how does quantization affect streaming token/sec?
01:52 - Carlos: yep kv cache = kv cache, although the transcript may say cash sometimes ha. kv cache reduces repeated compute for long contexts, so if you have many similar prefixes you save work. quantization reduces compute per token and helps throughput but can increase variance in quality; for streaming we see token/sec improve by 1.4-2x with 4-bit quantization on compatible models.
02:12 - Liu (Triton SRE): are you using Triton Inference Server internally? (small laugh) not to be confused w/our competitor. how does your runtime compare to Triton/Trt in terms of batching and kernel selection?
02:25 - Carlos: good question — our serving runtime compiles kernels and selects optimized paths based on seq-length distrib and hardware. continuous batching and dynamic microbatching helps keep latency low while improving token/sec. we also support per-route batching policies, and can configure max tokens per batch to keep p95 predictable. for POC we can test both our hosted config and a dedicated GPU pool to compare.
02:50 - Maya: what's your realistic p95 for 512 tokens on a dedicated A100 equivalent? we have customers that need 512 tokens at p95 <400ms ideally.
03:02 - Carlos: for 512 tokens, p95 <400ms is aggressive; on dedicated A100 class with optimized kernels and 4-bit quant we can approach ~350-450ms depending on model. on hosted shared pools p95 tends to be higher due to multi-tenant variance. we can run token/sec benchmarks with your prompt set to give concrete numbers.
03:20 - Ravi: concurrency math — if each request is 350ms p95 and we have 100 concurrent, we need to ensure enough GPU capacity. do you provide guidance for concurrency sizing?
03:33 - Carlos: yes we provide sizing recommendations: e.g., for a given model/quantization and target p95 we map to number of GPUs and reserved qps per GPU. we also expose autoscaling and burst lanes for Dedicated. common approach: start with a small dedicated pool sized for steady-state concurrency and enable burst to handle peaks. we can share a spreadsheet with assumptions.
03:50 - Sam: security check — we need SOC2, SSO (SAML), enterprise KMS integration and audit logs. Also VPC peering or private deployment options because we handle payments PII.
04:05 - Aisha (Redwood CSM): we have SOC2 and ISO docs, SAML SSO, and enterprise key management integrations. Private (VPC) deployments support customer-managed networking and HSM/KMS integration. we'll send the compliance pack.
04:18 - Maya: great. two more technical points: 1) streaming behaviour — do you do token-by-token model output or chunked flush? 2) fallback model plan if the larger model misses p95 under load.
04:33 - Carlos: we typically stream in small chunks (configurable flush interval) not strictly token-by-token to balance latency and overhead. fallback policies are supported — route to a smaller model variant or cached response. for critical SLOs some customers use a two-model strategy: a small low-latency model as primary and a larger quality model as secondary or asynchronous re-ranker.
04:55 - Ravi: about benchmarks, what do you need from us to run a realistic token/sec test?
05:02 - Carlos: sample prompt set, expected token lengths, concurrency profile (steady and burst), whether you need streaming semantics preserved, and any network topology constraints (VPC private). plus your quality thresholds so we can also measure regressions.
05:18 - Maya: we can provide a ~200 prompt set, typical token distribution and a simple UI replay harness. timeline: we'd like POC next week if possible.
05:30 - Lena: sounds doable. we'll run two benchmark tracks: Hosted with our recommended config and Dedicated with reserved capacity, and optionally Private if you want VPC. we'll return token/sec, p50/p95/p99 latencies, and streaming latency (time-to-first-byte and tokens/sec sustained).
05:47 - Sam: curious about cost tradeoffs — do you have ballpark per-token cost diff between hosted and dedicated?
05:55 - Aisha: yes we have examples: Dedicated reduces unit cost by 20-40% depending on utilization and quantization. we'll include sample cost calc in pricing doc.
06:06 - Liu: a operational question: if we do Dedicated, what's rollback behavior if a model rollout causes latency regressions?
06:13 - Carlos: we support canary rollouts and automatic fallback policies. you can pin traffic percentage and rollback automatically to the previous version or to a smaller variant. we also expose traces and token-level latency breakdown to diagnose regressions.
06:28 - Maya: network jitter concerns — for p95 under 300ms we need end-to-end numbers including network. can you run tests from our region and include e2e measurements?
06:41 - Carlos: yes we can run regional tests and recommend colocating the Dedicated pool in your cloud region; for Private we can deploy in your VPC for minimal e2e network. we'll note the region in benchmark plan.
06:55 - Ravi: for streaming, the guiding metric for our UX is time-to-first-token <120ms and sustained token/sec >= 25 tokens/sec per connection. can your hosted offering hit that with 512-token responses?
07:09 - Carlos: time-to-first-token <120ms is possible on Dedicated with optimized startup paths and warming. hosted may hit it in many cases but less reliably under high multi-tenancy. sustained 25 tokens/sec depends on model and quant; smaller models easily reach that, large LLMs may be lower unless quantized or sharded.
07:28 - Maya: Ok, so immediate asks: send benchmark checklist, security docs, pricing + sizing spreadsheet, and schedule POC kickoff with SEs and our infra team.
07:40 - Lena: we'll send all that. are there any other blockers for you to run a POC?
07:46 - Maya: mostly legal review for data handling and getting a test account in your Hosted sandbox or dedicated trial capacity.
07:53 - Aisha: we can provision a sandbox account and a limited Dedicated trial for POC. legal we can loop in — we'll send the standard DPA and info.
08:02 - Sam: one more — competitor question: we compared to Anthropic + Anthropic infra and some self-hosted options; what do you see as the main difference?
08:12 - Carlos: differences: ease of ops + unified API and rollouts vs self-hosting; cost/latency predictability and SLAs vs pure hosted commodity APIs; and tooling for cost/perf controls (batching, caching, quant profiles) compared to general cloud endpoints. we can share benchmarking examples versus OpenAI/Anthropic if you want.
08:32 - Ravi: noted. ok let's recap next steps.
08:35 - Lena: recap: 1) Redwood to send benchmark checklist, pricing & sizing spreadsheet, SOC2/compliance pack, and sandbox access. 2) Triton to share prompt set, concurrency profile and confirm POC date. 3) Schedule 1-hr POC kickoff with Carlos + Ravi + Liu + Maya.
08:55 - Maya: thanks, looking forward.
09:00 - Meeting end.

Notes: transcript includes occasional mis-hearings (kv cache sometimes transcribed as kv cash), filler words and small overlaps. Benchmarks and exact numbers to be produced in follow-up POC report.
